case.title: Removing the lead puts the work order in its normal place in Unassigned
case.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as an Owner or Admin user whose role has Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit, at {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
  • Your browser window is at least 1024 px wide, so the display switcher (List, Tech View, Board View) shows at the right of the Work Orders toolbar.
  • Technician {Technician-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha) is an active staff member at {Location-A} with Time Clock on and a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User.
  • Customers {Customer-A} to {Customer-D} are used by this case only, their names start with the same words (for example "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Unassigned Place") and end, in name order, with Alpha Co, Bravo Co, Charlie Co and Delta Co.
  • Approved work orders (for example S10043-17731 to S10043-17734): {Work-order-1} (for {Customer-A}) and {Work-order-3} (for {Customer-C}) are led by {Technician-A}; {Work-order-2} (for {Customer-B}) and {Work-order-4} (for {Customer-D}) have no lead technician.
  • Nobody has reordered work in Unassigned at {Location-A}.
  • No technician has a shift on the Schedule for these work orders.
  • On the Work Orders page nothing is ticked in Status, Asset on Site shows no choice (if its chip shows Yes or No, click the x on the chip), Assigned to me is off and Search is empty.
case.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders from the top menu and click the All tab.
  2. Type the shared start of the customer names (for example ZZAUTOTEST F3 Unassigned Place) in Search.
  3. Click Board View in the display switcher.
  4. Read the order of the Unassigned column.
  5. Hover {Work-order-3}'s card in {Technician-A}'s column and click its More actions (…) button.
  6. Click Unassign.
  7. Read the order of the Unassigned column.
  8. Open {Work-order-1}, clear its Lead Technician on the work order page, then go back to Work Orders > All > Board View with the same search.
  9. Read the order of the Unassigned column.
  10. Click Tech View in the display switcher and read the Unassigned group.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 4: Unassigned reads {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-4}.
  • Step 6: the message "{Work-order-3} moved to Unassigned" shows, with an "Undo" button.
  • Step 7: Unassigned reads {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}. {Work-order-3} takes its normal customer-name place, not the bottom.
  • Step 9: Unassigned reads {Work-order-1}, {Work-order-2}, {Work-order-3}, {Work-order-4}. {Work-order-1} is first by customer name, not at the bottom.
  • Step 10: Tech View's Unassigned group shows the same order.

Source — where this behaviour comes from

Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S9-R14, S2-R6 and S4-R5, read 19 Oct 2026. In version 53 (15 Oct 2026) S2-R6 was reworded to spell out the List's tie-break; the expected results are unchanged. Starting order (customer name A to Z): Review Decisions page 853901313, DR-45 (29 Sep 2026). The PRD of 7 Oct changed the removal rule (DR-47 had put a removed work order at the bottom of Unassigned); this case follows the PRD. In versions 66 to 68 (19 Oct 2026) the lead technician dialog stopped offering Unassigned (on the board the lead is removed with Unassign in the More actions menu) and the message became "{work order number} moved to Unassigned", with Undo; steps 5 and 6 and the step 6 result follow. Source-verified 19 October 2026. Not yet checked against a build in this wording. Re-read against PRD version 82 (29 Oct 2026) on 2 Nov 2026: the quoted rules are unchanged.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S9-R14: “A work order that gets a new lead from the lead technician dialog (Assign or Reassign lead technician) or from its detail page goes to the bottom of the new technician’s work, for everyone at the location, in both views. A work order dragged to a technician goes where it is dropped. Removing the lead with the menu’s Unassign action (S11-R9) or on the detail page puts the work order in Unassigned in the initial sort, not at the bottom, so it is not lost behind every other unassigned work order. Going to the bottom applies only to work moved onto a technician. A work order created or split off with a lead keeps the initial sort (S9-R3).”
  • S2-R6: “Before a manual order is saved, use the List’s default work order sort, ties included, exactly as the List sorts today: work orders for the same customer go by start date, newest first. The List itself does not change. A work order that gets a new lead after it was created goes to the bottom of that technician’s work instead (S9-R14).”
  • S4-R5: “After a successful lead change on Board View or Tech View, whether by drag, the dialog or Unassign, show the design’s toast (white, with the check icon) with an Undo button. It reads “{work order number} assigned to {technician name}”; “{work order number} lead technician set to {technician name}” when the new lead was already the technician on at least one of the work order’s lines; or “{work order number} moved to Unassigned” after removing the lead. Examples: “S1-357 assigned to Esther Howard”, “S1-702 lead technician set to Ralph Edwards”, “S1-352 moved to Unassigned”. This replaces the standard success toast for these messages only.”

Last checked against build v26.43.5-77de68c (production) on 11/2/2026.

  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043). Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher).
  • Role: Owner/Admin. On a QA branch sign in with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView". The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders). This user is the dispatcher.
  • Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location. Every technician and work order below belongs to this location.
  • Technicians (examples, the expected results call them by first name or full name): "ZZAUTOTEST Ana Alpha". A staff member counts as a technician when, in Settings > Staff > the staff member's edit icon > Edit Staff Member, they are Active, Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customers (used by this case only, each with one contact and one asset): "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Unassigned Place Alpha Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Unassigned Place Bravo Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Unassigned Place Charlie Co", "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Unassigned Place Delta Co". The steps and expected results call them by the end of the name ("Alpha Co", "Bravo Co", "Charlie Co", "Delta Co").

  • Nobody has reordered work in Unassigned at this location (if unsure, use a new location: Settings > Locations, with the technician enrolled there).

  2. For each: top menu Customers > New Customer, Name > Save; on the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact); then the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2) > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  3. Create each work order listed in the Preconditions: Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. Set the lead technician before invoicing. Once the work order is Approved, pick the technician in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page (leave it as Unassigned for an unassigned one). (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Write down each work order number as you create it (e.g. S1-801); the steps call each work order by the end of its customer name (e.g. "Alpha Co").
  4. Check the setup worked: Work Orders > All tab > List > type "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Unassigned Place" in Search — exactly 4 work orders show, all Approved: Alpha Co and Charlie Co led by Ana, Bravo Co and Delta Co with no lead; Board View's Unassigned column reads Bravo Co, Delta Co. If anything differs, correct that work order (status or Lead Technician) before starting.

  • Step 6: Unassigned reads Bravo Co, Charlie Co, Delta Co. Charlie Co takes its normal customer-name place, not the bottom.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10052 (Story 9, Drag to reorder work and technician groups/columns); SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S9-R14, S2-R6, S4-R5, read 8 Oct 2026. A work order dragged to a technician goes where it is dropped. Removing the lead from the Reassign lead technician dialog or the detail page puts the work order in Unassigned in the initial sort, not at the bottom, so it is not lost behind every other unassigned work order. Going to the bottom applies only to work moved onto a technician. A work order created or split off with a lead keeps the initial sort (S9-R3).”

  • S4-R5: “After successful reassignment, show “Lead technician updated”; after unassigning, show “Lead technician removed”.”
